title: Add release metadata endpoint + build-time metadata file for Private builds
author: Devon Price
description:
## Context
Offline signed bundles (Redwood Private) now rely on a stable identifier to correlate: (1) the signed bundle manifest, (2) the installer’s verification/audit events, and (3) support tooling (support bundle + bundle inspection output). During pilot we had multiple “what exact build is this cluster running?” moments because the running control-plane version alone wasn’t enough to disambiguate rebuilds/RCs.

This PR introduces a single “build identifier” (`private_build_id`) and exposes it in two ways:
1) a small HTTP endpoint on the Private control-plane API that returns release metadata (intended for internal/support tooling, and for customer environments that allow local HTTP access), and
2) a build-time generated metadata file (`release-metadata.json`) included in Private build artifacts so offline tooling can read it without any network.

## What’s included
- New release metadata shape (v1):
  - `schema_version`: "v1"
  - `private_build_id`: stable identifier used in signed bundle manifest `bundle.build_id`
  - `git_sha`: commit SHA
  - `build_time_utc`: RFC3339 timestamp
  - `channel`: `stable|rc|nightly`
  - `bundle_version`: semantic bundle version (if set by pipeline)
- API endpoint:
  - `GET /api/private/release-metadata`
  - returns JSON with the above fields
  - explicit cache headers: `Cache-Control: no-store` (we’ve seen proxies cache “version endpoints” in customer networks)
- Build-time generation:
  - new build step writes `dist/private/release-metadata.json`
  - included in packaging output consumed by private bundle builder
- Wiring for audit/support:
  - adds `private_build_id` to the existing “system info” payload used by support bundle generation (so Support doesn’t need cluster access + git)

## Why both endpoint + file
- Air-gapped: support tooling may only have the bundle tarball, not a running cluster.
- Connected private/VPC: querying the cluster is simplest and avoids “what artifact was used to install?” confusion.

## Security / access considerations
- Endpoint is intended to be served only on the existing authenticated API surface. No anonymous endpoint is added.
- No customer secrets or environment configuration is returned.
- `private_build_id` is treated as non-sensitive but still useful for correlation; we avoid leaking internal build pipeline URLs.

## Implementation notes
- `private_build_id` is sourced from `REDWOOD_PRIVATE_BUILD_ID` when present (release pipeline), otherwise defaults to `<git_sha>-dev` for local builds.
- Canonical JSON generation for the file is stable across runs given the same env vars (keys ordered, UTF-8, LF), to avoid downstream signature instability when the file is included in the bundle.

## Tests
- Unit tests for env var parsing + defaulting behavior.
- Handler test for `GET /api/private/release-metadata` covering auth required + response shape.
- Golden-file test for generated `release-metadata.json` (schema v1).

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Teach `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect` to display `private_build_id` from bundle metadata if present (tracked in ENG-4826).
- Document the field in the signed manifest spec once the manifest schema PR lands.

## Checklist
- [x] No new anonymous endpoints
- [x] Stable schema versioning (`schema_version: v1`)
- [x] Added tests
- [x] Updated internal release packaging docs (comment in build script + README pointer)

Related: ENG-4822 (pipeline signing step), ENG-4826 (support tooling).

test(private): add handler tests + golden output for metadata file
chore(docs): note build id env var and schema v1
changed_areas: dist/private/release-metadata.json (generated in CI; added as example fixture)
ci_summary:
Buildkite: ✅ build (linux/amd64) · ✅ unit tests · ✅ lint · ✅ api handler tests · ✅ packaging smoke test
Notes: initial run failed golden due to timestamp formatting; fixed by normalizing RFC3339 + injecting deterministic time in tests.
review_conversation: Connor O'Brien: Can we guarantee the JSON file output is deterministic? We can’t afford signature churn due to key ordering or whitespace.
Devon Price (author): Yep — file writer uses canonical encoder (sorted keys, no trailing spaces, LF) and the tests enforce it. `build_time_utc` is injected in tests; CI uses pipeline timestamp.
Jordan Lee: Please version the schema explicitly. We’ll want to evolve fields without breaking older installers/support tooling.
Devon Price (author): Added `schema_version: v1` and a small struct wrapper; endpoint + file both emit v1.
Ethan Park: Endpoint path naming — prefer keeping it under `/api/private/*` and require existing auth middleware.
Devon Price (author): Adjusted route to `GET /api/private/release-metadata` and confirmed it’s behind authn in the router.
Logan Wright: If this goes into support bundles, make sure it’s redaction-safe and doesn’t include hostname/cluster IDs.
Devon Price (author): Only build identifiers and git SHA; no environment identifiers included.
merge_outcome: Merged (squash) by Connor O'Brien into main; will ship with the next Redwood Private release train cut that includes signed offline bundles.
